C or U: B2 [ C or U ] the way that something or someone is thought of by other people

C: › [ C ] specialized literature a mental picture or idea that forms in a reader's or listener's mind from the words that they read or hear
B2 [ C ] any picture, especially one formed by a mirror or a lens
（尤指鏡子或透鏡形成的）鏡像；影像；映射

example: I have an image in my mind of how I want the garden to be.
我對花園該是甚麼樣子心裡有數。
He doesn't fit (= he is different to) my image of how an actor should look.
他和我心裡想的演員模樣並不相符。
The aim is to improve the public image of the police.
目的在於改善警察的公眾形象。
The company has made strenuous attempts to improve its image in recent years.
公司近年來作出了極大的努力來改善自身形象。
He's terribly image-conscious (= tries to dress and behave in a way that other people will admire).
他非常在意自己的形象。
The poem is full of images of birth and new life.
詩中充滿了誕生和新生活的意象。
television images of starving children
受飢兒童的電視畫面
The image you see in the mirror.
你在鏡子中看到的影像

NONE: › the use of words or pictures in books, films, paintings, etc. to describe ideas or situations

C or U: B1 [ C or U ] the ability to form pictures in the mind

U: › [ U ] something that you think exists or is true, although in fact it is not real or true

example: My younger son has a very vivid (= active) imagination.
我的小兒子想像力很豐富。

我從來都不會編故事——我根本沒甚麼想像力。

由於某種原因，這件事引起了公眾的關注。
It couldn't by any stretch of the imagination be described as a (= it is certainly not a) beautiful city.
這座城市再怎麼說也稱不上漂亮。
There's a sex scene in the film which apparently leaves nothing to the imagination (= shows sexual parts of the body very clearly).
這部電影中有一個十分露骨的性愛場面，沒有留下任何想像的餘地。
Was she paying him a lot of attention or was it just my imagination?
她是特別注意他呢，還是這一切只是我的臆想？
Is it my imagination or is David behaving strangely at the moment?
是我的錯覺呢，還是大衛現在真的是行為古怪？
It's a job that needs someone with a bit of imagination.
做這項工作需要有一點創造力。

NONE: C1 new, original, and clever

C1 good at thinking of new, original, and clever ideas
想像力豐富的，有創意的

example: an imaginative new approach/policy

NONE: B1 to form or have a mental picture or idea of something
想像；設想
B2 to believe that something is probably true
猜想，猜測
B1 to think that something exists or is true, although in fact it is not real or true
誤以為
› used to express shock or surprise, often at someone else's behaviour
（常用來表示對他人行為的驚訝、震驚）難以想像
› used to emphasize a statement
（表示強調）你無法想像

example: Imagine Robert Redford when he was young - that's what John looks like.
想像一下勞勃‧瑞福年輕時的樣子——那就是約翰的模樣。
[ + (that) ] Imagine (that) you're eating ice cream - try to feel how cold it is.
設想你在吃霜淇淋——試著感受一下它有多麼冷。
[ + question word ] Can you imagine how it feels to be blind?
你能想像失明的感覺嗎？
[ + -ing verb ] She imagined herself sitting in her favourite chair back home.
她想像自己正坐在家中最喜歡的扶手椅上。
They hadn't imagined (= expected) (that) it would be so difficult.
他們沒想到會這麼難。
I can't imagine (= I really don't know) what he wants from us.
我想不出他想從我們這裡得到些甚麼。
[ + (that) ] I imagine (that) he's under a lot of pressure at the moment.
我猜想他現在承受的壓力一定很大。
I don't imagine (that) they have much money.
我想他們不會有很多錢。
"Will they change it?" "I imagine so."
「他們會改變它嗎？」「我想會的。」
"Did you hear a noise?" "No, you're imagining things/No, you must have imagined it."
「你聽見甚麼動靜了嗎？」「沒有，你聽錯了吧／沒有，你一定是聽錯了。」
I've never heard her criticize you - I think you imagine it.
我從來沒有聽過她批評你——我想你在胡思亂想。
She got married at 16! Imagine that!
她16歲就結婚了！不可思議！
[ + -ing verb ] Imagine spending all that money on a coat!
花那麼多錢買一件大衣，真是匪夷所思！
You can't imagine what a mess the house was in after the party.
你簡直想像不到聚會之後屋內有多亂。
